originality.rationale: The closest source states the random Jacobi polynomial projection norm and high-probability rates but does not derive the sharp fixed-degree far tail. Royen and the published n=3 Beta-variance result already cover sample-variance small-ball phase exponents; they do not determine the sample-mean-weighted affine projection stability constants for all n. The new contribution is the exact joint-geometry amplitude, not the prior unweighted exponent.
residual_risks: An unlocated stronger theorem for joint sample mean/variance small-ball asymptotics with moving threshold may imply the constants.
The endpoint exponents and critical logarithmic mechanisms are previously established for sample variance; these are not counted as independent novelty.
One trigonometric sampling condition-number predecessor was inspected only at abstract level, and its different setting is not a complete exclusion.

value.rationale: Quantifies the exact catastrophic conditioning tail of the established degree-one Jacobi least-squares projection and gives sharp finite-moment criteria, including nontrivial minimal sample sizes for finite mean and variance. Exact leading constants quantify both interior cluster locations and singular endpoint competition rather than routine loose bounds. Value is limited to degree one/fixed beta parameters; there is no claim for general polynomial degrees or noisy reconstruction.
